finding_type: Unauthenticated GraphQL Introspection + Widget Token Generation + Internal Endpoint Leakage

confirmed_issues.title: Unauthenticated GraphQL Introspection on Sandbox
confirmed_issues.description: Full schema (43 mutations, 39 queries) exposed without authentication. Includes sensitive operations: registerUser, initiatePasswordlessLogin, createOrder, submitCddFormAnswer, addDepositTravelRuleDetails.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Introspection query returns complete __schema with all types and fields
confirmed_issues.impact: Full API surface enumeration enabling targeted attacks

confirmed_issues.title: Unauthenticated Widget Bootstrap Token Generation
confirmed_issues.description: openTopperWidget query generates valid signed JWT bootstrap tokens without any authentication. Token sub claim is constant (aa47e88b-59ca-404c-9171-7f5d9a6c18b6) across all calls, suggesting shared/static identity.
confirmed_issues.evidence: 3 consecutive calls returned identical sub claim with unique jti values. JWT decodes to valid claims structure.
confirmed_issues.impact: Potential widget session hijacking or unauthorized widget embedding if tokens are accepted by production or shared backend

confirmed_issues.title: Internal Engineering Endpoints Leaked in Widget HTML
confirmed_issues.description: Widget HTML source contains references to internal AWS and Kubernetes endpoints: graphql-server.topper-graphql-api.enterprise.engineering-development.uphold.aws, graphql-server.topper-graphql-api.backoffice.engineering-development.uphold.aws, graphql-server.topper-graphql-api.svc.cluster.local
confirmed_issues.evidence: Regex extraction from widget HTML body (145KB). DNS resolution fails externally but names reveal internal architecture.
confirmed_issues.impact: Internal infrastructure disclosure aiding further reconnaissance

confirmed_issues.title: Client Configuration Exposure via __NEXT_DATA__
confirmed_issues.description: Widget HTML exposes runtime configuration including SSO client IDs (Apple: com.topper.sandbox.sso, Google: 448034342668-l5si0uuf3cnas5sp6099t2u8ncdj5jhd), analytics endpoints, RiskJS public key reference, and Oscilar SDK URL.
confirmed_issues.impact: Third-party integration fingerprinting and potential SSO misconfiguration testing surface

negative_findings: Mutations (registerUser, createOrder, etc.) return generic operational error - backend may be partially down or require specific context
me() query returns null without auth error - no direct user data leakage confirmed
Internal endpoints not externally resolvable - no direct access confirmed
uncertainties: Whether sandbox shares backend/database with staging or production
Whether constant sub claim in widget tokens represents a service account or misconfiguration
Whether widget bootstrap tokens are accepted by production widget infrastructure
Whether operational errors on mutations indicate disabled functionality or missing prerequisites
recommendation: Report TP-001 through TP-004 as informational/low-medium findings on sandbox scope. Request clarification on sandbox vs production parity. Do NOT attempt destructive testing or token reuse against production.
next_steps_if_approved: Submit report to Intigriti Uphold program with all four findings bundled
Request program owner clarification on sandbox scope eligibility
If sandbox is out of scope, pivot to remaining Uphold assets: api-sandbox.uphold.com, portal.enterprise.uphold.com, GitHub repos

tp001_introspection.sandbox_result: HTTP 200 - Full schema exposed (43 mutations, 39 queries)
tp001_introspection.production_result: HTTP 400 - Introspection disabled by Apollo Server
tp001_introspection.assessment: Sandbox-only misconfiguration. Per program policy, sandbox findings must be reproducible in production to be valid. This finding alone would likely be closed as informational or out-of-scope.

tp002_widget_tokens.sandbox_result: Unauthenticated JWT generation with static sub claim
tp002_widget_tokens.reproducible_in_production: UNKNOWN - Requires active token replay against production widget which is out of scope per safe harbor
tp002_widget_tokens.assessment: Cannot verify production impact without active testing against production widget endpoint. The constant sub claim suggests service identity rather than user session, reducing severity even if accepted.

tp003_internal_endpoints.sandbox_result: AWS/K8s endpoint names leaked in widget HTML
tp003_internal_endpoints.dns_resolution: All internal endpoints fail external DNS resolution
tp003_internal_endpoints.reproducible_in_production: UNLIKELY - Production widget served via Cloudflare, different build pipeline expected
tp003_internal_endpoints.assessment: Informational at best. Internal naming convention disclosure without actionable access path.

tp004_next_data_config.sandbox_result: SSO client IDs and SDK URLs exposed
tp004_next_data_config.reproducible_in_production: POSSIBLE - Client-side configs often shared between environments
tp004_next_data_config.assessment: Low severity. SSO client IDs are semi-public by design. No secret material confirmed.

overall_production_parity: FAILED - Primary finding (TP-001) not reproducible in production
submission_recommendation: DO NOT SUBMIT in current form. Sandbox-only findings explicitly excluded per program policy. Pivot to production-scoped assets or new program.

pivot_targets.notes: Enterprise portal with Next.js login - test auth flows, IDOR, role escalation
Enterprise API backend - test auth bypass, parameter tampering
Secret scanning, CI/CD misconfigs, dependency vulnerabilities
